main.commit_message:
fix: support --help flag for subcommands

Add support for displaying help text when --help, -h, or other help flags
are used with subcommands. For example, `cargo xtask bench --help` now
properly displays help for the bench subcommand instead of treating it as
an unknown flag.

The fix integrates help flag detection into the subcommand parsing workflow
in `handle_subcommand_field()`. When a help flag is detected after a
subcommand name, the parser generates subcommand-specific help text using
the existing `generate_subcommand_help()` function and returns it via a
HelpRequested error.

This enables a better user experience where:
- `program --help` shows top-level help
- `program subcommand --help` shows subcommand-specific help
- Nested subcommands like `program sub-one sub-two --help` also work

Fixes #1324

fix: adapt to breaking changes in dependency updates

- Update datatest-stable macro from v0.2 to v0.3 format
- Handle quick-xml v0.38 API changes:
  - Replace BytesText::unescape() with decode()
  - Add Event::GeneralRef handling for entity references
  - Implement proper entity resolution for both named (<, >) and numeric (
, 	) entities
- Fix text concatenation logic to preserve entity-resolved characters

The quick-xml 0.38 update introduced a new event type (GeneralRef) for
entity references, which are now reported separately from text events.
This requires explicit resolution of both named XML entities and numeric
character references.

fix: export all targets in perf-data.json, show main, fix legend font

- Export all benchmark targets (not just facet_format_jit) so ratios
  can be computed on the frontend
- Remove filter that excluded main from branch list in app.js
- Add CSS to force Iosevka font on Observable Plot legends

fix: remove mode toggle and fix type errors

- Remove unused mode toggle links from benchmark reports
- Fix type mismatch in perf-index-generator
- Clean up dead code (filename() and other() methods)

gh-readonly-queue_main_pr-1327-a2c2d165a.commit_message:
feat: add support for decoding floats in msgpack

There's the potential for nuance based on how floats are cast. I figured
it was fine that f32 gets cast up to f64 when parsing, then back down to
f32 when being placed into the partial. By IEEE 754 specification, there
should be no issues - it's just moving bits around; the bits themselves
aren't truncated in any way. The odd case is when a type is f32, but it
is decoded from an f64. In that case, edge cases like
`f32::MAX != (f64::MAX as u32)` may occur, which may be reflected in
msgpack structures generated by systems that only support
double-precision floats. In that case, there's two (acceptable) options:
throw a type error, or parse a valid f32 and ensure the value being cast
down to f32 and up to f64 does not change the value, in which case, the
f32 variant may be safely returned. Two tests have been added to reflect
this behavior: successfully parsing a f32, and a FloatOverflow when a
f64 can't be represented as an f32.

- Export all benchmark targets (not just facet_format_jit) so ratios
  can be computed on the frontend
- Remove filter that excluded main from branch list in app.js
- Add CSS to force Iosevka font on Observable Plot legends

fix: rename time to value in bench report charts

The charts now display instruction counts, not time measurements.
Updated field names and axis labels to reflect this:
- ChartPoint.time -> ChartPoint.value
- BarPoint.time -> BarPoint.value
- X-axis label: 'Time (µs)' -> 'Instructions (K)'
